scenario: After 6 wrong passwords, even the right password is blocked for 15 minutes
steps: Enter a wrong password 6 times, then the correct one
actual: attempts 1-6: ['Incorrect email or pas', 'Incorrect email or pas', 'Incorrect email or pas', 'Incorrect email or pas', 'Incorrect email or pas', 'Incorrect email or pas']; 7th (correct): Too many attempts. Please wait 15 minutes and try again."}]

scenario: Changing the X-Forwarded-For header does not reset the login limit
steps: After being blocked, send the next attempt with a different X-Forwarded-For header
fix: Key the limit on the email alone as well as the IP, and only trust X-Forwarded-For set by your own reverse proxy (take the right-most trusted hop). Consider a persistent store so limits survive restarts.
remarks: The key is 'IP|email' and the IP is read straight from the client-supplied X-Forwarded-For header, so an attacker can rotate it on every request.

scenario: An expired session (older than 8 hours) is refused

remarks: Token forged with the local QA secret to simulate the 8-hour expiry without waiting.

scenario: A valid token for an account that no longer exists is refused
steps: Use a signed token with an unknown admin id

scenario: After signing out, a copy of the old session cookie no longer works
steps: Sign in, copy the cookie, sign out, then reuse the copied cookie
actual: old cookie STILL opens the dashboard
fix: Store a per-admin 'sessionVersion' (or a server-side session id) and bump it on logout and on password change; reject tokens with an old version.
remarks: Sessions are stateless HMAC tokens valid for 8 hours. Logging out only deletes the browser cookie. A stolen cookie keeps working until it expires, even after a password change.
